cluster_summary: These vulnerabilities arise from insufficient validation of external inputs (HTTP headers) and lack of uniform responses in password reset and email verification flows, leading to user enumeration, token leakage, and resource abuse.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled redirect targets, callback URLs, return URLs, OAuth redirect_uri values, or browser navigation destinations into redirect responses, Location headers, OAuth/OIDC/SAML redirect validation, or browser-followed navigation targets. Report code paths where the redirect target is accepted without constraining the final scheme and destination to trusted browser-safe values. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 4 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should validate redirect targets with an explicit safe-scheme and destination allowlist after decoding and normalization.

mechanism.missing_guard: the redirect target is accepted without constraining the final scheme and destination to trusted browser-safe values
mechanism.name: open redirect through unsafe URI scheme validation
mechanism.sink_shape: redirect responses, Location headers, OAuth/OIDC/SAML redirect validation, or browser-followed navigation targets
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled redirect targets, callback URLs, return URLs, OAuth redirect_uri values, or browser navigation destinations
mechanism.typical_fix: validate redirect targets with an explicit safe-scheme and destination allowlist after decoding and normalization

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Make the response uniform regardless of user existence: always return the same HTTP status code, message, and redirect target.
sub_patterns.name: User enumeration via distinguishable HTTP responses
sub_patterns.root_cause: The password reset or email verification endpoint returns different HTTP status codes, response messages, or redirect targets based on whether the user exists or has an email configured, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to enumerate valid user identifiers.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Introduce a configured base URL or trusted hosts list, and validate the header against it before using it in link generation; reject requests where the header does not match.
sub_patterns.name: Unvalidated HTTP header in email link generation
sub_patterns.root_cause: The application constructs URLs for password reset or email verification emails using the HTTP Host or Origin header from the incoming request without validating that the header matches a trusted domain, allowing an attacker to inject a malicious domain and cause token leakage or open redirect.
